notes.title: Tsukuyomi Content Update - July 13th
notes.content:
[b]Tsukuyomi, New Weapons, Armor Set, New Serial Hunt Quests[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043405/7e588ad9a562087db95e46de4b4eb80654e46dc4.jpg[/img]
Have you been keeping your skills sharp? How about your equipment; is it ready for anything? Tsukuyomi, a new light-devouring kemono, is hurtling towards Azuma. Before the end of this relay, it is likely to have already arrived. Remember to hide your fear, Tsukuyomi will not be an amenable opponent.

In today’s content update, the new Tsukuyomi descends into Fuyufusagi Fort, bringing with it materials for new weapons and an armor set. This month’s content update also introduces four new Serial Hunt Quests that feature entirely Mighty and Volatile kemono. You’ve got your work cut out for you this month.

Read more about the new content:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043405/9b23f253ce286d27745a9b6bf370527d3d808e61.png[/img]
[b]New Kemono - Tsukuyomi[/b]
A new light-devouring kemono—Tsukuyomi—has appeared at Fuyufusagi Fort. If you are to defeat this tyrannical territory seeker, you must bring all your hunting skills and knowledge to bear against it.

“Specter of the Eclipse” is the ominous moniker the Tsukuyomi has earned, but why? Does the sun hide behind the moon, or does this beast devour light itself? For it appears to feed not on Celestial Thread, but on rays of sunlight. And though it's said not to tussle with other kemono over territory, few creatures can survive without the sun's light. Mankind included.

The Tsukuyomi absorbs light in order to fuel its attacks. When you notice it starting to muster energy, try to send it reeling by use of a Pounder, Firework, or similar karakuri. Then strike as it resumes its energy build-up. Just remember that it's extremely resilient to physical strikes, so be wise and seek to bolster your attacks by elemental means.

[b]New Serial Hunt Quests[/b]
Four new Serial Hunt quests have been added to the Side Stories section of the Main Map. These four new quests exclusively feature Mighty and Volatile Kemono. We do not expect these to be easy, so prepare yourself for a grizzly challenge!

If you’ve yet to take on any of the Serial Hunts, here’s a quick refresher on how they work: On Serial Hunts, you’ll be forced to hunt a gauntlet of Kemono, each within a set period of time. While you’ll be able to quickly gather yourself in between hunts, hunters will be unable to draw from healing water wells.

Each time you successfully take down a target, your reward increases. However, if you fail at any stage of the hunt, you’ll receive no reward at all. Hunters may choose to end the hunt early in order to at least receive any rewards promised up to that point.

In addition to the rewards from each round, successfully taking down all targets in a single run will grant new Chat Stamps and Emotes.

[b]Highlighting Dolby Atmos & DTS:X[/b]
While already included in the first release, we wanted to highlight the amazing work that has been done by the team to incorporate Dolby Atmos and DTS:X as audio options. Dolby Atmos and DTS:X—both spatial, or three-dimensional, surround sound—enhance each and every sound found in the world of Azuma, allowing you to become completely immersed in each hunt.

When Dolby Atmos and DTS:X are enabled, here are just a few of the transcendent moments you can experience:
●	The roars of the giant kemono, including squeaking sounds of the plants and minerals that coexist in their bodies, and the flapping of the wings of aerial kemono flying overhead, will all become more three-dimensional, further enhancing the enormity of each kemono.
●	While it is easy to understand the mechanics of the Fireworks karakuri, you will feel it in your bones when they are launched into the sky, even if they detonate outside of your field of vision.
●	Hear native Japanese birds chirping and insects buzzing; each adding to the realism and instantly transporting you to one of Japan’s four seasons.

[b]Composers of WILD HEARTS[/b]
A wide variety of composers have worked on the music of WILD HEARTS: 

Masashi Hamauzu's music beautifully expresses the majestic nature of WILD HEARTS. From the title screen, Minato's daily hubbub, Deathstalker's hunt, various music during exploration, to other beautiful music that blends in with the surrounding nature of Azuma.

Daisuke Shinoda's powerful Japanese-style orchestral music adds excitement to the Lavaback, Golden Tempest, Sporetail, Ripclaw, and Murakumo hunts, as well as for the Deeply Volatile Kemono hunts.

Combined with the powerful Japanese-style sounds created by Koei Tecmo's composers (Junya Ishiguro, Ippo Igarashi, Modanqing Zhu), the magnificent performances of a wonderful orchestra, Japanese instrumentalists, and singers all come together to weave a vibrant world. 

Stay safe and stay sharp hunters!

notes.title: WILD HEARTS Patch - June 20th, 2023
notes.content:
[u][b]Improvements, Balance Adjustments[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] Custom dyes can now be preserved when saving loadouts in the Change Equipment menu.

[list]
[*] Fixed an issue that allowed the Celestial Anchor Karakuri to be used more times than intended.

[*] Fixed an issue where, in rare cases, the subtitle color setting was not reflected in the game.
[*] Fixed an issue that in rare cases caused the game to crash after a long period of play.
[*] Fixed and improved miscellaneous issues.
[/list]

notes.title: Update Notes: Alpha Sapscourge

[list]
[*] The attribute values of weapons and the resilience of armor can now be enhanced through the Limit Break system.
[*] An option to change Inherent Skills has been added to the Limit Break system. Inherent Skills can be added and replaced by consuming materials. This option will be unlocked after completing the main storyline and after you acquire your first Core Orbs.

[list]
[*] Hunted the target Volatile Kemono;
[*] Completed post-Chapter 3 quests, including the Recondite quests, in which the original species of the volatile Kemono was the hunt target.
[*] Players who have already completed the above criteria before the application of the update will only need to complete one of the conditions.
[/list]
[*] [For PC] Added new "DLSS" and "DLSS Quality" options that reduce the drawing load while maintaining high resolution to the Upscaling setting. These options are only available for GPU that support them.

notes.title: Content Update: Alpha Sapscourge
notes.content:
Alpha Sapscourge, New Weapons, Armor Set, Ornament, New Trial Quests, New Ways To Limit Break

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043405/b201c5d25f739daec6165bcb6e8431651161abc7.png[/img]

The trees and flowers are blossoming, the birds are overhead chirping, and the unique smell of spring is in the air! We are solidly into the allergy season. Or wait… that might just be the new Alpha Sapscourge scattering sap and pollen everywhere in our May content update that went live today. Either way, we’re all losing our Surprise Attack bonuses after a sneezing fit.

The new Alpha Sapscourge variant rolls into Harugasumi Way with new weapons, an armor set, and a new earring ornament modeled after the mysterious Tsukumo, all made from Alpha Sapscourge materials. This month’s content update also adds a plethora of quests. From the entirely new Trial quests, to hunts that target specific Volatile Kemono.

The Limit Break system has had its limits broken! Weapons and armor can now have their Attribute power and Resiliency enhanced, respectively. Inherent Skills are also able to be changed or added.
Read more about the new content:

[b]New Kemono Variant - Alpha Sapscourge[/b]
There have been frequent sightings in Azuma of a Kemono that boasts remarkable vitality, and brims with celestial thread, which it commands at will. By successfully hunting such a beast, you could surely obtain first-rate materials to forge new weapons and armor.
After completing the main story quest, you’ll be tasked with dispatching the Sapscourge in a new Side Stories quest called “Alpha Amber Rogue”.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043405/212f33aa9dc221a82b3adc925ad6d1d062e77cf1.png[/img]

[b]New Quests - Trial Quests, New Volatile Kemono Quests[/b]
While on a new Trial quest, hunters will be required to take on Kemono equipped with predefined armor, skills, and weapons. Test your skills as a hunter within these spartan constraints to see how swiftly you can triumph.

Trial quests do not require you to own any of the equipment, making them great opportunities to try out builds you’re less familiar with before investing gold and materials into new equipment. Rewards for successfully completing a Trial Hunt improve the faster you subdue your target.
Trial Quests will be added to Chapters 4 and 5.

Quests featuring specific Volatile Kemono have also been added from Chapter 3 to Side Stories. To unlock these quests, specific conditions must be met.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043405/8709fedf1321fd125d0fdc00543b2e4d920c1234.png[/img]

[b]New Ways To Limit Break[/b]
Weapons and armor can now have their Attribute power and Resiliency enhanced, respectively, using Core Orbs. Just as with Attack and Defense Limit Breaking, the number of times you can carry out such enhancements, and the effects they have, are different for each piece of equipment.

Hunters will also be able to use Core Orbs to change or supplement a weapon’s Inherent Skills. New skills are decided at random based on the type of weapon. The weapon’s default Inherent Skills and currently attached skills are excluded from the selection. When receiving new skills, the resulting skills will top out at a value slightly less than any already attached Inherent Skill.

Weapons will also be eligible for a third Inherent Skill. Any skill in this third slot will be significantly lower. Consequently, skills with values below a certain level or skills without a value to start with cannot occupy the third slot.

Stay safe and stay sharp hunters!

notes.title: Rejoin the hunt with the new WILD HEARTS™ update*
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043405/42020aed4fd4b1165e21c674b5f51e83021f3d8e.png[/img]

Join the hunt for the dangerous Murakumo, a new species of Kemono. This beast's plethora of petal-manipulating attacks are a real menace. It courses through the air on platforms made of sakura blossoms, making counterattacking tricky. You'll need to make use of the newly awakened “Spinning Top” Karakuri to drive out this fiendishly beautiful sakura spirit. Once unleashed, the Spinning Top closes in on its prey to deliver a relentless assault. Whenever it hits Kemono or other obstacles, it gains both speed and power.

Check out the interview on the new WILD HEARTS™ update with the game directors Hirata and Edagawa: 

[b]Murakumo[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043405/1d71d1d6b491f559b3bdd42aa275714c3961eb57.jpg[/img]

[u]Why did you go for the fox for the new upcoming Kemono?[/u]
●	Hirata: [i]When it came to creating a Japanese-style hunting action game, the fox was a Kemono we really wanted to include. There are a number of ethnic groups that consider foxes to be spirits or monsters, but in Japan in particular, foxes are a very important part of our culture and beliefs. I am also a big fan of foxes, so I strongly insisted on including foxes as endgame content after the story was completed.[/i]
 
[u]How did you come up with this idea of mixing the fox with Sakura?[/u]
●	Hirata: [i]We wanted the fox to be special, so we wanted to give it characteristics that had never been seen in previous kemono. The key elements were cherry blossoms and lightning. We have various beasts fused with nature in the game, but none of them have cherry blossoms, the most prominent landmark in the spring area. In addition, there is a special term in Japanese for "spring thunder" that conveys the arrival of spring. Using these elements as a foundation, we created a kemono that combines a fox with cherry blossoms, and commands cherry petals and lightning.[/i]

[u]Can you share key tips to beat Murakumo?[/u]
●	Hirata: [i]Murakumo is a small-sized kemono that moves very quickly. It also has an abundance of tricky ways to attack the player, such as charging forward on cherry petals or using a wide variety of long-ranged attacks to corner the player. Although it may seem confusing at first, if you observe it carefully, you should be able to find an opening after some of their attacks, so do not be intimidated by its many quick moves. Also, Murakumo’s signature move, riding on cherry blossom petals, is a good time to try and use Karakuri to bring it down.[/i]

[b]Quest[/b]

[u]Can you share tips to be successful in the new quest?[/u]
●	Hirata:[i] Murakumo's attacks carry wind and wood elements. The particularly powerful attacks are wind-based, so I would suggest investing in armor with wind resistance. In addition, fire and flames are effective against Murakumo, so making weapons with fire properties should make fighting it much easier.[/i]

[b]New System Update[/b]

[u]Can you elaborate on these updates and how they will impact players’ journey?[/u]
●	Edagawa: [i]First, we made it possible to further enhance weapon and armor stats. This will allow for a wider range of builds, such as choosing to use weapons and armor with lower stats but more appealing skills. Also, in late April we plan to add a new system of quests called serial hunts. These will be challenging quests where players will hunt kemono one after another with limited lives and health recovery resources, with added tension of having to choose whether to take on the next kemono or give up and settle for the rewards they have received up until that point. You can get materials needed to strengthen yourself, as well as new stamps and emotes, so we hope you will enjoy this new challenge.[/i]

[u]What parts of the upcoming content drop are you the most excited to see players enjoy?[/u]
●	Edagawa: [i]I would have to say I’m most excited to see players take on the new kemono, Murakumo. I think the most attractive thing about this hunting game is that there will be new kemono added with updates. I also hope that you will try to challenge other kemono by using the new karakuri that you can obtain through the battle with Murakumo.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043405/79f8fbaa2a329f67aee4e68129fab787e4e717cd.jpg[/img]

[u]Can you tell us more regarding the latest PC patches?[/u]
●	Edagawa: [i]The April 6th update improved the performance for some CPUs. In addition, we have added support for FSR, an upscaling option that reduces the drawing load while maintaining high resolution and will help to resolve the frame rate issues that some players have been experiencing. This is not limited to the PC version, but we are continuing to work on fixes for various issues, including unexpected crushes, as well as some balance adjustments.[/i]

Later this month you can face off against the dire Deathhaze Gloombeak – a new breed of volatile Kemono. And take on “serial hunt” special quests, where you'll be forced to hunt a succession of Kemono, each within a set period of time. Between each individual hunt, you will not be able to collect Healing Water from the surrounding area. So with chances to recover limited, you'll need to pay close attention to your health. Each time you successfully down a target, your promised reward increases. However, if you fail at any stage of the hunt, you receive no reward at all.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043405/5c0a16b8221609fe6d1bf1526b487cb9bbec8def.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Update Notes: Murakumo - Improvements, Balance Adjustments
notes.content:
[b]Improvements, Balance Adjustments[/b]

[list]
[*] Added a "Camera Distance" setting that allows the player to adjust the in-combat distance of the player character and the camera.
[*] Added a setting to change the color of the speaker name displayed in subtitles. 
[*] Added an option to dismantle all Karakuri placed by guests from the Detailed Map.
[*] Added an option to dismantle Dragon Karakuri from the Detailed Map.
[*] Increased the reward for offering assistance by using a Hunter's Gate, as well as further increased the reward for assisting on story quests.
[*] The Stamina gauge will now flash when you do not have enough Stamina to perform an action.
[*] You can now use voice chat during loading screens.
[*] Icons for buffs obtained from skills or food will now appear for each individual buff, even if the icons are the same.
[*] An icon for the nearest campsite will now appear on the compass at the top of the screen.
[*] You can now check details for individual loadouts in the Forge.
[*] Adjusted the sorting order when sorting ingredients so that seasonings now are properly sorted together.
[*] While in the Karakuri Stance, player inputs will now prioritize the creation of Karakuri.
[*] Visiting hunters in Minato will now have their player name and ID displayed above their head. The display setting can be toggled on the chat wheel.
[*] Cladding will now be temporarily hidden when dying armor.
[*] The dye color will now be shown on the armor forging screen and the cladding production screen.
[*] It is now possible to check the overall number of tsukumo discovered in all areas by placing the cursor over Minato on the Main Map.
[*] It is now possible to collect materials and other items while riding on a Roller.
[*] It is now possible to eat in the middle of a hunt when hunting Giant Kemono.
[*] Food buffs will now not be reset after resting at a Hunter's Tent.
[*] It will no longer be possible to eat between the Final Blow of a hunt and traveling to a different area.
[*] Improved the camera lock-on to where it is less likely to unintentionally unlock during a hunt.
[*] The Flying Vine Dragon Karakuri is now easier to place in Minato, even in close proximity to a NPC.
[*] Added a notification for when there is a completed food processing item in Minato.
[*] The Paddle Scoop Karakuri will now return to its base when full.
[*] Attacks from the Training Bear Karakuri will no longer hit tsukumo.
[*] In specific cases when an area change is immediately triggered after defeating a Giant Kemono, broken off Kemono materials will automatically be added to the player's inventory.
[*] It is now possible to offer assistance on all quests from the Hunter's Gate located in Minato.
[*] When searching for an online co-op session to join for a particular hunt, if there isn't an exact match but other co-op hunting sessions with the same content are, the player will join one of the other co-op hunting sessions instead of finding no sessions at all. This applies to the following:
[list]
[*] Hunting Encore – Old Trail Tribulations: Search for "Hunting Song – Reverberations"
[*] Hunting Encore – Auspice of Minato: Search for "Hunting Song – Rising Glissando"
[*] Hunting Encore – Summit Strife: Search for "Hunting Song – Elegy"
[*] Volatile Spectral Tombtail: Search for "Volatile Kemono – Blossom Trail"
[*] Volatile Fervid Crazecomb: Search for "Volatile Kemono – Spirit Isle"
[*] Volatile Miasmic Grimquill: Search for "Volatile Kemono – Harvest Canyon"
[*] Volatile Lurid Soulstalker: Search for "Volatile Kemono – Frozen Fort"
[*] Deeply Volatile Laharback: Search for "Deeply Volatile Kemono — Ruins"
[*] Between Earth and Sky: Search for "Ocean Blaze Awakening"
[*] Blossoms of Oblivion: Search for "Remnants of Reverie""
[/list]
[*] Small Kemono will no longer initiate combat when the health of the Giant Kemono being hunted is below a certain threshold. Regardless of the Giant Kemono's health, Small Kemono will escape during combat with the following Kemono: Volatile Pearlbeak, Volatile Onyxshard, and Miasmic Grimquill.
[*] Adjusted Hunter Vision to make it better at guiding players to a target Kemono.
[*] Added a "Dye" tutorial.
[*] Improved visibility of Talismans placed throughout Azuma.
[*] Adjusted rain and snow effects.
[*] Improved the loading speed of some loading screens.
[*] Reduced the time it takes to change stances after deploying the Ki Base with the Hand Cannon.
[*] Increased the transition speed from Celestial Thread Charge to fortified firing stance with the Hand Cannon.
[*] Increased the standard firing rate of the Hand Cannon.
[*] Changed the following Hand Cannon action names:
[list]
[*] "Battō Aerial shot" → "Aerial Bombardment"
[*] "Aerial Bombardment" → "Heatwave Bombardment"
[/list]
[*] Hand Cannon's fortified shot can now be interrupted by placing Karakuri.
[*] It will now be easier to land attacks following a successful Bladed Wagasa's parry.
[*] Increased the power of attacks chained after Attack 1 immediately following a successful parry with a Bladed Wagasa.
[*] Sped up the Stamina recovery following a successful parry with a Bladed Wagasa.
[*] Increased the movement distance of Bladed Wagasa's Twenty Tatami Spit.
[*] Reduced Stamina consumption of the Karakuri Katana's Single-Handed Lunge, and increased its power and movement distance.
[*] Increased the transition speed from Aerial Downward Slash into Iai Slash Burst with a Karakuri Katana.
[*] Increased the speed of Karakuri Katana's Bamboo Cleave.
[*] Increased the gauge amount generated from Karakuri Katana's Iai Slash Burst.
[*] Increased the range of the Maul's Chaser Smash attack.
[*] Increased the speed and power of the Maul's Overhead Swing attack.
[*] Increased the speed of Maul's Jumping Smash, Extended: Jumping Smash, and Flame Smash attacks.
[*] Increased the power of the Power Smash attack performed with a fully-extended Maul.
[*] Decreased the number of Karakuri required before extension when the Expert Hitter skill is activated.
[*] Increased the power of Nodachi's Iai: Bisection.
[*] Increased the power of Nodachi's Iai: High Dive.
[*] Increased the power of Nodachi's Iai: Soaring Slash Streak.
[*] Increased the power, speed, and gauge build-up amount of Nodachi's Flaming Slash.
[*] Decreased the delay following the Running Slash attack with a Nodachi, and made it possible to follow up with another Running Slash in the same direction.
[*] Made it easier to transition into Downward Slash from Double Spin Slash with a Nodachi.
[*] Decreased the delay following the Celestial Stab attack with a Nodachi using the Crate Karakuri.
[*] Wingblade Spin Slash can now combo into Wingblade Crescent Slash.
[*] Wingblade Crescent Slash can now combo into Wingblade Spin Slash.
[*] Changed the requirements of the Turbulence: Fury and Turbulence: Body skills and increased their effect time.
[*] The claw gauge will now decrease when performing attacks with the claw lodged in.
[*] Increased the number of attacks required to trigger the reinforced state while attacking with the claw lodged in.
[*] Decreased the power of Claw Blade's Wingblade Spin Slash.
[*] Improved visibility when performing the Glider Karakuri attack with a Claw Blade.
[*] Increased the speed of the Slash Streak attack with a Karakuri Staff.
[*] Increased the number of arrows released at the end of the Burst: Haya attack with a Bow.
[*] Reduced the screen shaking during Burst: Haya and Volley: Haya.
[*] Made it easier to knock Kemono over with the Ephemeral Lightning Arrow skill.
[*] Adjusted to prevent Karakuri Thread recovery on resonance during attacks using the Basic Karakuri with a Bow.
[*] Increased the amount of Stamina consumed when dodging with a Bow.
[*] Reduced the dodge distance when using a Bow.
[*] Adjusted the movement of tsukumo companions.
[*] Adjusted the amount of Karakuri Thread each weapon generates when attacking Kemono.
[*] Added the following adjustments to the Celestial Anchor Karakuri:
[list]
[*] Reduced durability;
[*] Sliding dodge can now be performed with your weapon sheathed;
[*] Special sliding dodge can now be performed by canceling various actions with your weapon drawn.
[/list]
[*] Reduced the effect time of the Tangle ailment on players.
[*] Increased the effect time of the Tangle ailment on Kemono.
[*] Adjusted damage dealt from critical hits.
[*] Adjusted the Claw Blade tutorial. This can be accessed through Main Menu > Information > Tutorials.
[*] Adjusted the Bow tutorial. This can be accessed through Main Menu > Information > Tutorials.
[*] Made it easier for the player to have a flash of inspiration during the Fumebeak and Pearlbeak hunts.
[*] Made it easier for the player to have a flash of inspiration while hunting Golden Tempest.
[*] Adjusted the behavior of the Roller Dragon Karakuri.

[*] Increased damage dealt by the Pounder Karakuri.

[*] Increased the placement speed of the Firework Karakuri.
[*] Increased the healing amount of the Healing Mist Karakuri.
[*] Increased the damage dealt by the Pile Driver Karakuri. Additionally, fixed an issue where sometimes the Pile Driver Karakuri would be destroyed after multiple were placed.
[*] Changed the Basic Karakuri required to create the Celestial Shield Fusion Karakuri.
[*] Reduced the durability of the Celestial Shield Karakuri.
[*] It is now possible to topple Kemono multiple times by using the Celestial Cannon Karakuri.
[*] The Combat Vine Karakuri can now also be unlocked during a hunt with Mighty Icetusk.
[*] Changed the trigger condition of the Peril Promise skill to "when even a single player is near death".
[*] It is now possible to consume Healing Water even at full HP when the Nostrum Water or Miracle Water skills are active.
[*] The Mountain Felling Giant Blade skill now increases the power of Full-Body Slam and Full-Body Cleave when the mutation level of the Karakuri Staff is Maxed Out.

notes.title: Content Update 1 - 10 March
notes.content:
Welcome to the first post-launch content update for WILD HEARTS! In today’s content update, a new Kemono – the Hellfire Laharback – has been added, including a quest to face off against this fiendish foe and a new talisman skill. The Hellfire Laharback is sure to be a fiery challenge for those unprepared.

This content update also includes an ample amount of adjustments and fixes that the team has been working extremely hard on to improve the game and we wanted to take a moment to highlight those efforts. To callout just three of these fixes/improvements:
[list]
[*] Players now can look at their full list of skills equipped during armor creation, weapon creation, and armor modification.
[*] Fixed an issue that prevented players from receiving rewards after successfully hunting certain giant kemono.
[*] Karakuri that can contain food, such as Ingredients Chest and Drying Rack placed in advance, will be removed to ensure that they are not destroyed during the battle with Amaterasu in Minato.
[/list]

This, of course, isn’t the end, as we’re dedicated to Wild Hearts and we’ll be consistently working on making the gameplay experience better throughout this year for all our players to enjoy the game. Your feedback is invaluable so please continue to share your thoughts with us.

The new content coming today includes the following:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043405/1747d217012d90335bb7ae22ccd2297cc59d4d67.png[/img]

[b]New Kemono - Hellfire Laharback[/b]
A new breed of volatile Kemono – a Hellfire Laharback – has appeared on the Natsukodachi Isle. You must quell the torrid inferno before it reduces everything to ash, and restore tranquility to the island.

For accomplishing this new feat, hunters will receive the title Fire Fiend Appeaser.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043405/79aa38de610b6c9c365d807b7ec10061aa8997a6.png[/img]

Will you be able to handle the heat or will you back out of the hunt?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043405/7bb2585977566c0a08f3d3b4315e0d54762986c8.png[/img]

[b]New Talisman Skill - Infernal Blow[/b]
Upon your first successful hunt, Hellfire Laharback may drop a talisman with a new skill – Infernal Blow.

Infernal Blow will increase the chances of setting prey ablaze and boosts the power of attacks against ablaze Kemono.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043405/4d6b92e4a21bf78dffb00c0f9a17f8d9bd433e54.png[/img]

[b]New Quest - Deeply Volatile Kemono - Ruins[/b]
After you complete all the main story quests, Suzuran’s husband Yoshichi will have a new request for you. After accepting the quest, you will find the hunt on the Main Map under the new section Side Stories.

Side Stories will allow you to access any additional quests that are added via content updates.

[b]Grimstalker in Two Weeks, Murakumo & More in April[/b]
Still want more? In two weeks on March 23rd in a second content update this month, Grimstalker arrives in Azuma! After completing the quest for your first hunt, check out the new Grimstalker armor and weapons. To show our excitement, new emotes and chat stamps are also being added. 

Rumors also swirl that even more Kemono are on their way to Azuma in April. Until then, stay focused on the hunt in front of you.

*Requires WILD HEARTS (sold separately) and all updates to play.

notes.title: Wild Hearts review - crafty monster hunting
notes.content:
As a diehard Monster Hunter fan, I want to give Wild Hearts more of a chance. It's a gorgeous-looking action game in which you can fight creatively designed behemoths with some ridiculously powerful and, at times, unorthodox weapons. The monsters' savage attacks require you to use the game's unique Karakuri system to defend yourself. It has a lot of potential, and I want to like it so much more, but unfortunately, the performance issues - partially improved since launch, but still significant - make fights feel like trudging through a boggy swamp when they should be snappy and action-packed.

This is a massive shame because my experience with Wild Hearts has sometimes felt as fresh as my first time playing Monster Hunter World. You take the role of a nameless hunter who arrives in the Azuma region only to fall in battle against an icy wolf, one of the many Wild Hearts monsters, or 'Kemono'. As your hunter lays dying, a masked man seems to put something inside of them, enabling them to use long-forgotten Karakuri - ancient technology employed by hunters from years gone by to control the beasts.

notes.title: Discover Fusion Karakuri
notes.content:
Hear me Hunters!

Let's discover today: Fusion Karakuri. They require hunters to build multiple basic Karakuri that then fuse together, hence “fusion” Karakuri. These are intended for countering Kemono attacks, although they can be used in a variety of situations. To learn fusion Karakuri, hunters must seek new Kemono to battle. 

CELESTIAL SHIELD
This defensive Karakuri can be used in many situations, but its main purpose is to counter charge attacks or to simply be used as a wall to block a Kemono attack.

POUNDER
While it packs a wallop, the pounder is a more complex Karakuri that has a slower attack that inflicts a large amount of stun damage to its target.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043405/098676587dba06a6b5a7ad05421b3418d433e573.png[/img]

STAR BOMB
The star bomb boasts a high attack power alongside a wide attack range. Although it takes some time to detonate on its own, it’ll explode immediately when attacked. Be warned though, the blast can send your fellow hunters flying if they’re caught in the explosion!

REPEATER CROSSBOW
An offensive Karakuri that shoots at regular intervals to increase your damage output and distract Kemono for a few precious seconds. A great choice when hunting flying Kemono.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043405/4b84fc0f63e4670ccff09106b3e2a4f651284f5b.jpg[/img]

CHAIN TRAP
Kemono that fall prey to a hunter’s chain trap will be immobile for a short period of time. Be sure to use this Karakuri wisely, as Kemono will begin to figure out how to escape the trap faster with each use.

CELESTIAL CANNON
One of the most complex Karakuri, the celestial cannon collects surrounding celestial thread that it then hurls at its target. While difficult to aim, the cannon has such an intense impact that it has a chance to stagger Kemono.

[i][u]ECOLOGY [/u][/i]
A dangerous beast that will attack smaller Kemono or humans without discrimination. The Hanayadoshi, or Ragetail, is a voracious eater and is permanently hungry despite consuming vast amounts of food compared to its size. This may be due to nutrition being diverted by the fruit-like growth at the tip of its tail. It tends to ignore everything else when it's pursuing a meal, but if angered it will abandon the chase and attack.

notes.title: Discover Basic Karakuri
notes.content:
Hear me Hunters!

The Karakuri are an ancient technology that has sat dormant for years. While hunters of old once knew how to use Karakuri, that knowledge has been lost to time. That is, until you appeared. Use the Karakuri to stand toe-to-toe against Kemono, the giant nature-infused beasts that roam Azuma.

There is a long road ahead of you for mastering the many kinds of Karakuri. How you use them to enhance your abilities will be up to you, and new Karakuri are still being discovered by fellow hunters.

Karakuri can be broken down into three main categories, based on the way they interact with hunters and the world around them.

Let's discover today: Basic Karakuri. They are simple, quickly constructed and tend to do well during combat. They also generally do not require many resources to craft. 

CRATE 
The basic building block of the Karakuri. Allows hunters to gain the high ground to avoid attacks or, when positioned correctly, perform a powerful attack from above.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043405/6cae7415b4eaa4a1bfecb5e487ab9b9ac7d7fe43.png[/img]

SPRING
Launches the hunter in a desired direction. It can be crafted quickly and used to dodge, perform an enhanced jumping attack, or even flank a Kemono faster than one could on foot.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043405/26109fc55c8f7ba06176179e0c2ec75e89ccec6f.png[/img]

TORCH 
Useful both in and out of combat, the torch can be used to light a dimly lit area or to add fire to a hunter’s weapon to deal additional damage. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043405/de0f865051c5ac474063ef5604e551dceb90b8fb.png[/img]

GLIDER 
Can be used in conjunction with a wind vortex or even a few crate Karakuri, the glider allows hunters to stay in the air longer to traverse Azuma more easily or position yourself directly overtop a Kemono. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043405/e83b675d535a18894eb72514621ba88e0ef1926d.png[/img]

CELESTIAL ANCHOR 
Hunters can tether themselves to a celestial anchor and swing around the anchor to close the gap between them and a Kemono. Celestial anchors can be used in some non-combat situations as well. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043405/aa244a19b076758b355529a4086f2b58e2467c4f.jpg[/img]

Pre-purchase the Karakuri Edition today and join the hunt with all the extras including the Karakuri Samurai and Karakuri Ninja armor sets, a decorative Tsukumo Lantern, three Emotes, and five Chat Stamps.

notes.title: Discover Sapscourge
notes.content:
Learn more about your prey: SAPSCOURGE

[previewyoutube=NpNVpW_elOI;full][/previewyoutube]

ECOLOGY 
The Kohakunushi, or Sapscourge, produces substances very similar to pollen and sap from its craggy skin and shaggy fur, both of which have a distinctly woody appearance. However, the Kemono appears ill-equipped to deal with its own physiology, sneezing at the pollen it sheds and accidentally covering its prey in sap time after time, before clumsily attempting to wash it off.

STRATEGY 
If you're covered in the pollen that flies off this Kemono when it sneezes, you could black out. And if you're caught in its sap, you'll struggle to evade its onslaughts. So be very careful of any follow-up attacks. The tail is softer than it looks, and severing it will greatly reduce the beast's attack range, so you should focus on taking out your target piecemeal.

notes.title: WILD HEARTS Bestiary: Golden Tempest
notes.content:
WILD HEARTS™ is a unique twist on the hunting genre where technology gives you a fighting chance against fearsome beasts infused with the ferocious power of nature itself, known as Kemono. No one remembers why the Kemono began their rampage through a once prosperous Azuma. 
But hope arrives in the form of a formidable hunter, armed with deadly weapons and ancient technology, called Karakuri, that could turn the tide of battle. Take on these creatures alone or hunt with friends in seamless co-op.

Some travelers are wary of the wind. They're worried it might be a Golden Tempest that gives the wind its piercing howl. This terrifying creature has now been sighted in Azuma, migrating from a distant land. Far in the north, it's said there is a mysterious place known as the Golden Sea, where the sand stretches to the horizon in every direction. This is the homeland of the Aragane, or Golden Tempest. It’s a place where fools go in search of gold, never to return. This beast is the embodiment of the wind, which blows some to riches and others to their death.

Its powers come from the fusion of different natural elements – a strange mixture of tempestuous wind and precious flakes of pure gold. Its organs mysteriously produce the precious metal by compressing the air inside its body. As a rare creature that can create gold out of nothing, it is revered as a creature that brings wealth to those who see it.

Commanding the surrounding air, the Golden Tempest specializes in fighting by changing the direction of its own movement by blowing air out of the vents (stripes) located all over its body – allowing it, in a certain sense, to fly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043405/ced3611db7458493f8b72b9e5dd36368f6127911.png[/img]

Its fighting techniques combine powerful melee attacks with the strength of a gale. It specializes in taking control of the battle by using air currents to change both its own and hunters’ positions and movement speed. Staying alert and preparing for fast close combat are your surest path to success when taking on this beast.

Failing that, you will face the Golden Tempest’s attacks at full force: paw swipes, bite strikes, claws, spinning and slams. Come within range of any of these attacks and you will pay dearly.
But even from a distance, the beast is daunting. Beware its swinging tail and wind blades if you want to survive the battle.

If you live to see the Golden Tempest turn into its enraged state (generating wind around its body before blasting it away) you will be a witness to the truly ferocious beauty of nature. Marvel at a sparkling tornado of sand and gold, then experience the terror of being pinned to the ground by that same force. Golden Tempests are an especially beautiful sight when in combat, clad in a golden wind, and for many, a sight they will take with them to the afterlife.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043405/0bd5c343f573cd29cb699677274cfb93fbd31326.jpg[/img]

Use your weapons in combination with a wise selection of Karakuri to counter the Golden Tempest’s many avenues of attack. If this is still not enough, you may wish to consider something rather extreme, like a celestial cannon.

Players can now pre-purchase the WILD HEARTS Karakuri edition to receive unique in-game items: two full armor sets (Karakuri Samurai & Karakuri Ninja), a decorative Tsukumo Lantern, and three different emotes - including the Fighting Spirit, Grovel and Conch. They will also unlock the pre-purchase bonuses. The hunt begins February 17, 2023. Pre-purchase now!
